package_info.why_malicious: The package is a multi-stage dropper that loads and executes obfuscated payloads entirely in memory, bypassing disk-based detection. It is used to deliver a variety of final-stage malware (RATs, info stealers) and employs anti-analysis and anti-forensics techniques.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Extracts and loads a .NET PE DLL file directly into its current process using a runtime assembly object (Assembly.Load).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code extracts an embedded DLL resource, loads it directly into memory using Assembly.Load, and executes it, enabling in-memory execution of the next stage payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and executing code from memory without writing to disk is a common malware evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not load and execute obfuscated DLLs from embedded resources at runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packers or protectors may use in-memory loading for IP protection.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Decompresses an embedded gzip blob to extract another PE DLL and .NET library, then loads the next stage reflectively.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code decompresses an embedded gzip blob, extracts a new DLL, and loads it reflectively into memory, continuing the multi-stage payload chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Multi-stage decompression and reflective loading are used to evade static analysis and detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely chains multiple obfuscated DLLs in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some software updaters or protectors may use compressed resources.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Class 'Munoz' creates a copy of the executable in the temp folder and extracts/loads the next payload from a bitmap resource.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates a copy of itself in the temp directory, then extracts and reflectively loads the next stage payload from an obfuscated bitmap resource.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-replication and extracting code from image resources are anti-forensics and obfuscation techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not hide code in bitmap resources or replicate themselves in temp folders.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: De-obfuscates, reflectively loads, and executes the final payload (e.g., Lokibot, AgentTesla, Remcos, etc.) from memory.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code de-obfuscates and reflectively loads the final malware payload, which may perform credential theft, remote access, or other malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Final payloads are well-known malware families; reflective loading and obfuscation are used to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not load known malware families or use such obfuscation.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated hexadecimal strings in resources (e.g., replacing '0' with 'ZZ', 'F' with 'YY'), reversed at runtime and loaded as assembly code.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code de-obfuscates hexadecimal strings from resources, converts them to bytes, and loads them as assemblies for execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscating code as strings in resources and dynamic assembly loading are used to evade static analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not obfuscate and load code in this manner.
key_indicators: Dynamic assembly loading from de-obfuscated strings

attack_chain.action: User executes the dropper EXE (delivered via phishing/ISO).
Dropper extracts and reflectively loads the stage 2 DLL from embedded resources.
attack_chain.leads_to: Stage 2 DLL decompresses and loads stage 3 payload

attack_chain.action: Stage 2 DLL decompresses a gzip blob, extracts, and reflectively loads stage 3 DLL.
Stage 3 DLL creates a copy of itself in temp, extracts and loads stage 4 payload from bitmap resource.
Stage 4 DLL de-obfuscates and reflectively loads the final malware payload (RAT/stealer/etc.).
attack_chain.leads_to: Final payload executes (credential theft, remote access, etc.)

behavioral_signatures: Extraction and execution of code from obfuscated resources (bitmaps, strings)
Decompression and dynamic loading of embedded payloads
file_indicators: Embedded resources with obfuscated names (e.g., Kolko_i_krzyzyk, faLa, dZAu, JqZn)
Bitmap/image resources with high entropy or visual noise
DLLs with internal names: Hadval.dll, Pendulum.dll, cruiser.dll, Farinell2.dll, Discompard.dll
network_indicators: Connections to known C2 URLs (e.g., http://64.227.48.212/project/five/fre.php, http://171.22.30.147/tony/five/fre.php)
Network activity from in-memory loaded processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes that load multiple .NET assemblies from memory, especially when assemblies are extracted from obfuscated resources (bitmaps, strings) and never written to disk. Flag high-entropy or visually noisy embedded resources. Detect self-replication to temp directories and reflective loading of known malware families. Correlate with network connections to known C2 infrastructure.
